messages:
sarah: Heads-up: p99 on prod inference fleet spiked ~2.7x at 18:12 UTC after the CUDA 12.3.1 driver rollout. Observed Triton switched many calls from `flash_attn` -> `flash_attn_fallback` for small sequences, KV cache hit rate dropped, GPU memory climbed and we saw evictions. Investigating.
tanvi: @sarah can you attach kernel hist and a short profile? Which model/route hit this?
sarah: model: rdx-13b-chat@v2, route: hosted-us-east-1, traffic ~40k rps. Quick NVTX slice (truncated):
```
Kernel                 Calls   Total(ms)   Avg(ms)   Name
flash_attn_fallback    18234   18650.2      1.02      flash_attn_fallback
flash_attn            5123    620.1        0.12      flash_attn
attention_kernel_small 21034   40012.4     1.90      attn_small_seq
```
Notable: fallback calls jumped 3x at 18:07 and coincide with KV evictions.
liam: infra notes: driver rollout `cuda-driver/12.3.1` started at 18:05 UTC for pool-a. Some nodes were live-rebooted.
infra-bot: deploy: `cuda-driver/12.3.1` rolled to `pool-a` at 2025-10-05T18:05Z by deployer. Previous: `12.2.3`.
tanvi: hypothesis: kernel_selector uses reported `maxSharedMemoryPerBlock` and `smem` availability to pick flash kernel path. Driver 12.3.1 changed reported workspace limits for certain SM architectures, making selector prefer fallback on small sequences. Combined with KV thrash (more host<->GPU IO) we get p99 blowup.
sarah: KV logs show burst: `kv_cache_evictions: 1200` in 1m around spike start. Memory pressure triggers more kernel workspace allocations -> more fallback.
liam: telemetry shows a co-located tenant doing heavy PCIe transfers on 3 nodes at the same minute — possible noisy neighbor. PCIe saturation + new workspace behavior = double hit.
ops-kai: I'm moving the noisy tenant off those hosts and setting stricter cgroups. For immediate mitigation, can we force the runtime to prefer `flash_attn` again?
tanvi: we have a runtime override flag: `--force-kernel=flash_attn` in `serving.conf`. Risk: older drivers might actually produce illegal memory accesses if kernel assumptions are wrong. Safe approach: canary 5% traffic to nodes with override, compare p99/kv-hit. Command to patch rollout (example):
```
curl -X PATCH "https://ops-api.internal/v1/route/hosted-us-east-1" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"canary": {"percent": 5, "overrides": {"serving.conf": {"force-kernel": "flash_attn"}}}}'
```
sarah: launching 5% canary with override now. Monitoring metrics.
(some minutes)
sarah: Canary nodes show p99 back to baseline (~90ms -> 32ms), kv_evictions drop to normal. :thumbsup:
liam: opened escalate to driver team with DTrace/artifact: `INC-2025-412`. Also capturing `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi` around spike. dmesg had repeated: `nvlink: pci dma timeout` entries on a couple hosts.
ops-kai: incident ticket created: INC-2025-412. I'm keeping canary on while we coordinate with driver/infra. Will add host-level traces to ticket.
tanvi: follow-ups: 1) add unit tests for kernel_selector to simulate changed `maxSharedMemoryPerBlock`/workspace responses, 2) add a rollout gate that validates kernel histograms during driver upgrades, 3) add an alert for `kv_cache_evictions` spike > 250/min. I'll open PRs.
sarah: agree. Also adding a postmortem checklist item: capture kernel-selection snapshot during driver upgrades. Thanks all — will update when driver team responds. :eyes:
